objective: Define a PIT-safe integrated three-statement forecast architecture for stock-selection research without duplicating driver, free-cash-flow, scenario, project-economics or valuation modules.
corePrinciple: A three-statement model is a reconciliation and dependency engine, not an alpha vote by itself. It must transform PIT-valid operating and financing assumptions into mutually consistent income statement, balance sheet, equity roll-forward and cash-flow states while preserving explicit UNKNOWNs.

sourceAccountingFrame.taiwanIssuerFrame: FSC issuer financial-report regulations require a complete set including balance sheet, statement of comprehensive income, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows and notes, with FSC-endorsed IFRS/IAS as the accounting basis.
sourceAccountingFrame.ifrs18Transition: IFRS 18 applies for annual reporting periods beginning on or after 2027-01-01, permits earlier application, and is retrospective under IAS 8. Historical replay must version presentation/reclassification semantics rather than treating new subtotals as unchanged economic series.
sourceAccountingFrame.economicDriverFrame: Revenue growth, operating margin and reinvestment/capital efficiency are linked economic drivers; growth is not free and reinvestment must be economically consistent with the forecast growth path.

D07_20: cash/debt funding bridge and financing-plug disclosure
ownershipBoundary.D07_21: Owns revenue, gross/operating margin and OPEX driver formation; D07-20 consumes these assumptions and checks statement coherence.
ownershipBoundary.D07_22: Owns detailed working-capital, CAPEX and FCF forecast design; D07-20 integrates those outputs into statement reconciliation.
ownershipBoundary.D07_23: Owns scenario/sensitivity generation; D07-20 must replay each frozen scenario consistently but does not create a second scenario vote.
ownershipBoundary.D07_18: Supplies cost-of-capital primitives when valuation/financing comparisons require them; D07-20 does not recreate WACC as independent evidence.
ownershipBoundary.D07_19: Owns project economics and real options; project forecasts may feed D07-20 but must not be double-counted.
ownershipBoundary.D08: Consumes forecast outputs for valuation. Mechanical forecast closure must never create an independent valuation confirmation.

incomeStatement: Revenue and operating cost/expense assumptions produce operating profit under a versioned presentation mapping.
Interest/financing and tax assumptions bridge operating result to net income without hiding financing as operating economics.
balanceSheet: Operating working-capital accounts, PPE/intangibles, debt, cash, tax balances and equity roll forward from prior-period stocks and current-period flows.
Retained earnings reconcile beginning equity plus comprehensive/net-income and distribution/issuance effects under explicit accounting policy.
cashFlow: Operating, investing and financing cash flows reconcile beginning cash to ending cash.
Working-capital movements, depreciation/amortization, CAPEX/acquisitions, debt/equity financing and distributions cannot be silently omitted.
circularityPolicy: Interest-cash-debt circularity must be solved by a declared method or remain UNKNOWN; never hide it inside an unexplained plug.
A balancing plug may be diagnostic only and must identify economic funding source/constraint before use in research.

pitContract.asOfRule: Every historical forecast assumption must have knownAt/availableAt <= forecastDecisionAt. Management guidance, analyst consensus and model assumptions remain separately labeled.
pitContract.revisionRule: Later filings, guidance revisions, restatements and realized results append as later vintages; they never rewrite the ex-ante forecast used at the historical decision date.
pitContract.ifrs18Rule: IFRS 18 adoption/early adoption/reclassification is a presentation vintage. Historical economic comparisons require mapped comparable lines or explicit UNKNOWN, not naive line-item continuity.
pitContract.unknownRule: Missing driver, financing, tax or statement mapping remains UNKNOWN. Mathematical balancing cannot manufacture missing economics.

consistencyChecks: Assets = liabilities + equity within declared rounding tolerance.
Beginning cash + operating + investing + financing cash flow = ending cash.
Retained-earnings/equity roll-forward agrees with earnings, distributions, issuance/buybacks and OCI where modeled.
Revenue growth requiring capital must reconcile with working-capital/capacity/reinvestment assumptions rather than assuming free growth.
Operating-margin path must be explainable by price/mix/cost/scale inputs owned by D07-21.
Debt and interest paths must be mutually consistent with cash deficit/surplus and financing policy.
Depreciation/amortization and CAPEX/PPE roll-forward must not create impossible stock-flow paths.
falsification: Reject a model-quality claim when statements balance only because of an unexplained cash/debt/equity plug.
Reject forecast improvement created by later actual results, revised filings or restated classifications leaking into an earlier decision vintage.
Reject growth paths whose reinvestment/capacity requirements are economically inconsistent with revenue growth.
Reject margin expansion when it is only a presentation/reclassification effect or lacks identifiable driver support.
Reject apparent forecast alpha if it disappears after controlling for directly available earnings/consensus/current-fundamental/valuation information.
Reject promotion when success is concentrated in one industry, one reporting regime or one accounting presentation transition.
Treat exact three-statement closure as data-quality evidence, not proof that the forecast is accurate or that the stock is mispriced.
researchHypotheses: H1: Integrated reconciliation may reduce false-positive growth stories by exposing funding, reinvestment and working-capital inconsistencies.
H2: Forecast-consistency diagnostics may add more value as validation/downside-risk controls than as standalone directional alpha.
H3: The incremental value should be tested beyond simpler revenue-growth, margin, FCF, leverage and consensus-surprise primitives.
H4: Accounting-presentation transitions such as IFRS 18 can create false time-series breaks unless presentation vintages are normalized or explicitly marked.
H5: A forecast that balances mechanically but depends on a large unexplained financing plug should have lower research confidence, not a positive score.
taiwanPITReplayPlan: Use MOPS/TWSE/FSC-authoritative statement vintages and publication/authorization timestamps where available.
Replay at least several Taiwan issuers from materially different industries, including capital-intensive and asset-light cases.
Preserve original statements and later corrections/restatements append-only.
Record management guidance, external consensus and model-built assumptions as separate provenance lanes.
Include at least one case crossing a presentation/accounting-policy transition or reclassification boundary.

maturityDecision.rationale: Mechanism, cross-module ownership, PIT/revision semantics, accounting-presentation transition guard, reconciliation invariants and falsification are now explicit. Taiwan issuer historical PIT replay is not yet physically demonstrated, so L3 remains closed.

l3Gate: PIT replay for at least three Taiwan-listed issuers across at least two materially different industries.
Original financial-statement vintages and knownAt/availableAt evidence.
Management guidance, consensus and model assumptions separately tagged.
Append-only later revisions/restatements/actuals with no ex-post rewrite.
At least one financing/cash circularity or funding-constraint case and one accounting-presentation/reclassification case.
Demonstrated reconciliation without unexplained balancing plugs.
l4Gate: Common-support comparison versus simple revenue/margin/FCF/leverage/consensus baselines.
Forecast-error and missingness accounting with negative results preserved.
